course_description:
Students investigate a number of problems and applications that have a significant role in modern statistics. The course develops skills in writing and presenting statistics for general and specialist audiences.

This course comprehensively covers applied statistical methods with an emphasis on statistical modelling using both maximum likelihood and Bayesian theory and with a view to enabling a statistical expert to provide comprehensible statistical assistance to non-statistical clients. Topics to be covered include Monte Carlo methods, Bayesian inference, extensions of linear models to generalized linear models, generalized estimating equations and time series methods. Students will fit statistical models to data and perform analysis using R and/or Python; both are powerful, commonly used programming languages for statistical modelling and machine learning.

Our Inclusivity Champions are here to listen, to understand your concerns, and to explore potential actions that can be taken to resolve them. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

course_aims: The course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to perform statistical analyses on data with moderately complex distributional characteristics and sampling structure --- the type frequently encountered in scientific investigations across a broad spectrum of disciplines.

learning_outcomes.description: build an appropriate statistical model to represent the process generating the data.
apply likelihood based methods to problems of estimation and hypothesis testing.
apply regression diagnostics in order to verify model assumptions.
recognise the limitations of linear models and generalized linear models.
apply Monte Carlo methods and Bayesian statistics
use the statistical package R appropriately for the analysis and graphical representation of data.
communicate the results of statistical analysis clearly and accurately.
